column3: “He is flesh” preserves the concrete body term rendered “he is mortal.”
“In his generations” preserves the plural expression rather than “in his generation.”
Repeats “the earth” in the clause about being filled with violence.
“All flesh had corrupted its way” preserves the collective image and singular “way,” rather than “all living creatures … their ways.”
“All flesh” preserves the collective image of “all living creatures”; “destroying them with the earth” preserves the accompanying earth.
“Nests” preserves the image used for the “rooms.”
“Finish it to a cubit from above” does not explicitly supply “its walls”; the decks are called lower, second, and third.
“All flesh in which is the breath of life” preserves the collective body image of “every creature.”
“For you and for them” preserves the singular address and pronoun rather than “for yourselves and for the animals.”
The obedience is stated and then repeated: “so he did.”
